text: The 'rate problem' component of the problem of temporal passage (Section 39.1) is the objection that:
choices: specifying a rate of passage requires two independent units, yet 'one second per second' measures time against itself and so conveys no information
special relativity denies any frame-independent set of simultaneous events, so an objective 'now' cannot be defined
if the block grows, an observer cannot tell whether they are at its leading edge or at some earlier point already in the past
erasing the memory of an earlier moment dissipates at least k_B T ln 2 of heat, giving experience a thermodynamic direction
explanation: The rate problem observes that a genuine rate needs a second, independent temporal dimension; 'one second per second' is trivially uninformative because it measures time in terms of itself. Option 1 is the distinct presentism-relativity impasse, option 2 is the growing block's 'how do we know it is now now?' epistemological worry (Braddon-Mitchell), and option 3 is Landauer's principle — each a real topic in the unit, but none is the rate problem.
